style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MainStreet BankShares, Inc., (the &#8220;Corporation&#8221;, &#8220;MainStreet&#8221;, or &#8220;BankShares&#8221;), was incorporated in the Commonwealth of Virginia on January 14, 1999.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet was primarily formed to serve as a bank holding company. <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT>Its first wholly-owned subsidiary was located in Martinsville, Virginia and was sold on March 23, 2005.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In 2002, MainStreet organized a second bank subsidiary, Franklin Community Bank, National Association (&#8220;Franklin Bank&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On February 8, 2007, MainStreet formed a wholly-owned real estate company, MainStreet RealEstate, Inc., for the sole purpose of owning the real estate of the Corporation.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MainStreet is authorized to engage in any lawful activity for a bank holding company.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The holding company structure provides greater flexibility than a bank standing alone because it allows expansion and diversification of business activities through newly formed subsidiaries or through acquisitions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet&#8217;s business is conducted through its subsidiary bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Franklin Community Bank, N.A.</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Franklin Bank is a nationally chartered commercial bank and member of the Federal Reserve whose deposits are insured by the FDIC.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank opened for business on September 16, 2002.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank accepts deposits from the general public and makes commercial, consumer, and real estate loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank operates as a locally-owned and operated commercial bank emphasizing personal customer service and other advantages incident to banking with a locally owned community bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It relies on local advertising and the personal contacts of its directors, employees, and shareholders to attract customers and business to the Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank emphasizes a high degree of personalized client service in order to be able to serve each customer.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank&#8217;s marketing approach emphasizes the advantages of dealing with an independent, locally managed commercial bank to meet the particular needs of individuals, professionals and small to medium-sized businesses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The main office of Franklin Bank is located at 400 Old Franklin Turnpike, Suite 100, Rocky Mount, Virginia.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank has banking offices located at 12930 Booker T. Washington Highway, Hardy, Virginia and 25 Southlake Drive, Union Hall, Virginia.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank&#8217;s primary service area is Franklin County, Town of Rocky Mount and surrounding areas.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For the most part, Franklin Bank&#8217;s business activity is with customers located in its primary market area.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Accordingly, operating results are closely correlated with the economic trends within the region and influenced by the significant industries in the region including pre-built housing, real estate development, agriculture, and resort and leisure services.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Much of the market area is considered rural; however, the resort surrounding Smith Mountain Lake attracts many tourists to the area.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MainStreet RealEstate, Inc.</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MainStreet RealEstate, Inc. was formed for the sole purpose of owning the real estate of the Corporation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It now owns the facility in which Franklin Bank&#8217;s Southlake&#160;office operates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Competition</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Franklin Bank experiences competition in attracting and retaining business and personal checking and savings accounts, making commercial, consumer, and real estate loans and providing other services in their primary service area.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The principal methods of competition in the banking industry for deposits are service, rates offered, convenience of location, and flexible office hours.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The principal methods of competition in the banking industry for loans are interest rates, loan origination fees, and the range of lending services offered.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Competition in the service area comes from other commercial banks, savings institutions, brokerage firms, credit unions, and mortgage banking firms.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Competition for deposits is particularly intense in Franklin Bank&#8217;s market which increases the cost and reduces the availability of local deposits.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Because of the nature of Franklin Bank&#8217;s market, a substantial portion of the loan opportunities for which banks compete are real estate related.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>During the present economic downturn, which has been focused on real estate, the number of loan opportunities has been reduced and the risk of those loans has been increased.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank has been able to take advantage of the consolidation in the banking industry in our market area by providing personalized banking services that are desirable to large segments of customers, which has enabled the bank to compete satisfactorily.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We intend to continue to provide a high level of service with local decision-making focused solely on our local market.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We process daily by branch capture, a method by which checks are processed by tellers rather than item processing, which allows for better efficiencies along with all day banking.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We also receive and send our cash letters electronically.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, a new online business module will be implemented in 2014, which will allow our business banking clients to have more control over their accounts.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We believe these factors more than offset the advantages that larger banks in our markets may have in offering a larger number of banking locations and broader range of services.</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Regulation, Supervision and Government Policy</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">BankShares and Franklin Bank are subject to state and federal banking laws and regulations that provide for general regulatory oversight of all aspects of their operations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As a result of substantial regulatory burdens on banking, financial institutions like MainStreet and Franklin Bank are at a disadvantage to other competitors who are not as highly regulated, and MainStreet and Franklin Bank&#8217;s costs of doing business are accordingly higher.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A brief summary follows of certain laws, rules and regulations which affect MainStreet and Franklin Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Recent and expected changes in the laws and regulations governing banking and financial services could have an adverse effect on the business prospects of MainStreet and Franklin Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The current economic environment has created uncertainty in this area, as legislators and regulators attempt to address rapidly changing problems which are likely to lead to new laws and regulations affecting financial institutions.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MainStreet BankShares, Inc.</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MainStreet is a bank holding company organized under the Federal Bank Holding Company Act (&#8220;BHCA&#8221;), which is administered by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (&#8220;Federal Reserve&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet is required to file an annual report with the Federal Reserve and may be required to furnish additional information pursuant to the BHCA.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Federal Reserve is authorized to examine MainStreet and its subsidiaries.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>With some limited exceptions, the BHCA requires a bank holding company to obtain prior approval from the Federal Reserve before acquiring or merging with a bank or before acquiring more than 5% of the voting shares of a bank unless it already controls a majority of shares.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On June 17, 2009, MainStreet entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (&#8220;MOU&#8221;) with the Federal Reserve which was amended effective January 26, 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The MOU was terminated in September 2013 and there are no longer restrictions or stipulations attributable to the MOU.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Refer to Item 7, Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis for a detailed discussion.</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Bank Holding Company Act</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under the BHCA, a bank holding company is generally prohibited from engaging in nonbanking activities unless the Federal Reserve has found those activities to be incidental to banking.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Bank holding companies also may not acquire more than 5% of the voting shares of any company engaged in nonbanking activities.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Virginia Banking Act.</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Virginia Banking Act requires all Virginia bank holding companies to register with the Virginia State Corporation Commission (&#8220;Commission&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet is required to report to the Commission with respect to financial condition, operations and management.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Commission may also make examinations of any bank holding company and its subsidiaries.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (&#8220;GLBA&#8221;) permits significant combinations among different sectors of the financial services industry, allows for expansion of financial service activities by bank holding companies and offers financial privacy protections to consumers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>GLBA preempts most state laws that prohibit financial holding companies from engaging in insurance activities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>GLBA permits affiliations between banks and securities firms in the same holding company structure, and it permits financial holding companies to directly engage in a broad range of securities and merchant banking activities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet is not a financial holding company.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Sarbanes-Oxley Act</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT>The Sarbanes-Oxley Act (&#8220;SOX&#8221;) enacted sweeping reforms of the federal securities laws intended to protect investors by improving the accuracy and reliability of corporate disclosures.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It impacts all companies with securities registered under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, including MainStreet.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>SOX creates increased responsibilities for chief executive officers and chief financial officers with respect to the content of filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Section 404 of SOX and related Securities and Exchange Commission rules focused increased scrutiny by internal and external auditors on MainStreet&#8217;s systems of internal controls over financial reporting, which is designed to insure that those internal controls are effective in both design and operation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>SOX sets out enhanced requirements for audit committees, including independence and expertise, and it includes stronger requirements for auditor independence and limits the types of non-audit services that auditors can provide.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Finally, SOX contains additional and increased civil and criminal penalties for violations of securities laws.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT>&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <TABLE
style="WIDTH: 100%">
    <TR>  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="left">
</TD>
  <TD
style="FONT-STYLE: normal; WIDTH: 34%; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" align="middle">
2</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="right">
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD><BR /></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 2px solid; FONT-STYLE: normal; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; HEIGHT: 1px; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 1px" contenteditable="false">
</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On October 14, 2008, the U. S. Treasury announced the Troubled Asset Relief Program (&#8220;TARP&#8221;) under the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In the program, the Treasury was authorized to purchase up to $250 million of senior preferred shares in qualifying U. S. banks, savings and loan associations, and bank and savings and loan holding companies.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The amount of TARP funds was later increased up to $350 million.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The minimum subscription amount was 1% of risk-weighted assets and the maximum amount was the lesser of $25 billion or 3% of risk-weighted assets.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet did not participate in TARP.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009&#160;(&#8220;ARRA&#8221;)</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The ARRA was enacted in 2009 and includes a wide range of programs to stimulate economic recovery.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, it also imposed new executive compensation and corporate governance obligations on TARP Capital Purchase Program recipients.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Because MainStreet did not participate in TARP, it is not affected by these requirements.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act</I></FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Dodd-Frank Act was signed into law on July 21, 2010.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Its wide ranging provisions affect all federal financial regulatory agencies and nearly every aspect of the American financial services industry. <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT>Among the provisions of the Dodd-Frank Act that directly impact the Corporation is the creation of an independent Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, (&#8220;CFPB&#8221;), which has the ability to write rules for consumer protections governing all financial institutions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>All consumer protection responsibility formerly handled by other banking regulators is consolidated in the CFPB.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It will also oversee the enforcement of all federal laws intended to ensure fair access to credit.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The CFPB has begun implementing mortgage lending regulations to carry out its mandate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Even though Franklin Bank did not participate in the activities which precipitated the crisis these new rules have the effect of increasing the processing time and cost for making residential mortgage loans and from a practical standpoint limiting the residential mortgage loans Franklin Bank will make.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, the Federal Reserve issues new rules, effective October 1, 2011, which had the effect of limiting the fees charged to merchants by credit card companies for debit card transactions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Dodd-Frank Act also contains provisions that affect corporate governance and executive compensation.</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Although the Dodd-Frank Act provisions themselves are extensive, the full impact on the&#160;Corporation of this massive legislation continues to be unknown.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Act provides that several federal agencies, including the Federal Reserve, the CFPB and the Securities and Exchange Commission, shall issue regulations implementing major portions of the legislation, and this process is ongoing.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Jumpstart Our Business Startups (JOBS ACT)</FONT></I><FONT style="COLOR: black; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On April 5, 2012, the President signed the Jumpstart our Business Startups (&#8220;JOBS&#8221;) Act into law.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The objective of the legislation, as the name implies, is to stimulate the growth of small to midsized companies through facilitated access to capital and reduced regulatory reporting requirements. This, in turn, is expected to create jobs as businesses use this newly infused capital to expand operations. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Franklin Community Bank, N.A.</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Franklin Bank is a national banking association incorporated under the laws of the United States, and the bank is subject to regulation and examination by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (&#8220;OCC&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank&#8217;s deposits are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) up to the limits of applicable law.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The OCC, as the primary regulator, and the FDIC regulate and monitor all areas of Franklin Bank&#8217;s operation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These areas include adequacy of capitalization and loss reserves, loans, deposits, business practices related to the charging and payment of interest, investments, borrowings, payment of dividends, security devices and procedures, establishment of branches, corporate reorganizations and maintenance of books and records.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank is required to maintain certain capital ratios.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It must also prepare quarterly reports on its financial condition for the OCC and conduct an annual audit of its financial affairs.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The OCC requires Franklin Bank to adopt internal control structures and procedures designed to safeguard assets and monitor and reduce risk exposure.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>While appropriate for the safety and soundness of banks, these requirements add to overhead expense for Franklin Bank and other banks.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On April 16, 2009, Franklin Bank entered into a formal agreement (&#8220;Agreement&#8221;) with the OCC.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Franklin Bank has achieved full compliance with the agreement, which was terminated in August of 2013.</FONT> </FONT>Refer to Item 7, Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis for a detailed discussion.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Community Reinvestment Act</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank is subject to the provisions of the Community Reinvestment Act (&#8220;CRA&#8221;), which imposes an affirmative obligation on financial institutions to meet the credit needs of the communities they serve, including low and moderate income neighborhoods.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The OCC monitors Franklin Bank&#8217;s compliance with the CRA and assigns public ratings based upon the bank&#8217;s performance in meeting stated assessment goals.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Unsatisfactory CRA ratings can result in restrictions on bank operations or expansion.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank received a &#8220;satisfactory&#8221; rating in its last CRA examination by the OCC.</FONT></DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition to other consumer privacy provisions, the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA) restricts the use by financial institutions of customers&#8217; nonpublic personal information.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At the inception of the customer relationship and annually thereafter, Franklin Bank is required to provide its customers with information regarding its policies and procedures with respect to handling of customers&#8217; nonpublic personal information.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>GLBA generally prohibits a financial institution from providing a customer&#8217;s nonpublic personal information to unaffiliated third parties without prior notice and approval by the customer.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The USA Patriot Act</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The USA Patriot Act (&#8220;Patriot Act&#8221;) facilitates the sharing of information among government entities and financial institutions to combat terrorism and money laundering.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Patriot Act imposes an obligation on Franklin Bank to establish and maintain anti-money laundering policies and procedures, including a customer identification program.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Bank is also required to screen all customers against government lists of known or suspected terrorists.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>There is additional regulatory oversight to insure compliance with the Patriot Act.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Consumer Laws and Regulations</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>There are a number of laws and regulations that regulate banks&#8217; consumer loan and deposit transactions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Among these are the Truth in Lending Act, the Truth in Savings Act, the Expedited Funds Availability </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Act, the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, the Fair Housing Act, the Fair Credit Reporting Act, and the Fair Debt Collections Practices Act.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank is required to comply with these laws and regulations in its dealing with customers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, the CFPB has begun adopting rules regulating consumer mortgage lending pursuant to the Dodd-Frank Act.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>There are numerous disclosure and other compliance requirements associated with the consumer laws and regulations.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Deposit Insurance</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank has deposits that are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>FDIC maintains a Bank Insurance Fund (&#8220;BIF&#8221;) that is funded by risk-based insurance premium assessments on insured depository institutions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Assessments are determined based upon several factors, including the level of regulatory capital and the results of regulatory examinations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>FDIC may adjust assessments if the insured institution&#8217;s risk profile changes or if the size of the BIF declines in relation to the total amount of insured deposits.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In 2013 and 2012, Franklin Bank paid $196,501 and $253,874, respectively, in FDIC assessments.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It is anticipated that assessments may increase in the future to offset demands on the BIF from banks that fail in the troubled economy.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Such increases could adversely affect the Bank&#8217;s profitability.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On October 3, 2008, the FDIC announced that deposits at FDIC-insured institutions would be insured up to at least $250,000.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It was extended to December 31, 2013, and then permanently.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">FDIC announced its Transaction Account Guarantee Program on October 14, 2008.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Transaction Account Guarantee Program, which is a part of the Temporary Liquidity Guarantee Program, provides full coverage for non-interest bearing deposit accounts of FDIC-insured institutions that elected to participate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank elected to participate in this program and opted to continue in the program.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>There were increased BIF assessments for program participants.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This program has terminated.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">After giving primary regulators an opportunity to first take action, FDIC may initiate an enforcement action against any depository institution it determines is engaging in unsafe or unsound actions or which is in an unsound condition, and the FDIC may terminate that institution&#8217;s deposit insurance.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Capital Requirements</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Federal Reserve has adopted risk-based capital guidelines that are applicable to MainStreet.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The guidelines provide that the Corporation must maintain a minimum ratio of 8% of qualified total capital to risk-weighted assets (including certain off-balance sheet items, such as standby letters of credit).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At least half of total capital must be comprised of Tier 1 capital, for a minimum ratio of Tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets of 4%.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, the Federal Reserve has established minimum leverage ratio guidelines of 4% for banks that meet certain specified criteria.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The leverage ratio is the ratio of Tier 1 capital to total average assets, less intangibles.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet is expected to be a source of capital strength for its subsidiary bank, and regulators can undertake a number of enforcement actions against MainStreet if its subsidiary bank becomes undercapitalized.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet&#8217;s bank subsidiary is well capitalized and fully in compliance with capital guidelines.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, regulatory capital requirements relate to earnings and asset quality, among other factors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Bank regulators could choose to raise capital requirements for banking organizations beyond current levels.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As discussed in Item 7, Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis, MainStreet&#8217;s subsidiary bank entered into a formal agreement with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency which contained requirements relative to Franklin Bank&#8217;s capital levels.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank has achieved full compliance with the agreement, which was terminated in August 2013.</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"></FONT>&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On July 2, 2013, the Federal Reserve voted to adopt final Basel III capital rules for U. S. banking organizations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The final rules establish an integrated regulatory capital framework and will implement in the United States the Basel III regulatory capital reforms from the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and certain changes required by the Dodd-Frank Act.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under the final rule, minimum requirements will increase for both the quantity and quality of capital held by banking organizations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Consistent with the international Basel framework, the final rule includes a new minimum ratio of common equity tier I capital (Tier 1 Common) to risk-weighted assets and a common equity tier I capital conversation buffer of 2.5% of risk-weighted assets that will apply to all supervised financial institutions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The rule also raises the minimum ratio of tier I capital to risk-weighted assets and includes a minimum leverage ratio of 4% for all banking organizations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These new minimum capital ratios will become effective for MainStreet on January 1, 2015 and will be fully phased in on January 1, 2019.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The final rule emphasizes common equity tier I capital, the most loss-absorbing form of capital, and implements strict eligibility criteria for regulatory capital instruments.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The final rule also improves the methodology for calculating risk-weighted assets to enhance risk sensitivity.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Banks and regulators use risk weighting to assign different levels of risk to difference classes of assets.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Failure to meet statutorily mandated capital guidelines or more restrictive ratios separately established for a financial institution could subject the Bank or MainStreet to a variety of enforcement remedies, including issuance of a capital directive, the termination of deposit insurance by the FDIC, a prohibition on accepting or renewing brokered deposits, limitations on the rates of interest that the institution may pay on its deposits and other restrictions on its business.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As described above, significant additional restrictions can be imposed on Franklin Bank if it would fail to meet applicable capital requirements.</FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Limits on Dividend Payments</I></FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As a national bank, Franklin Bank may not pay dividends from its capital, and it may not pay dividends if the bank would become undercapitalized, as defined by regulation, after paying the dividend.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Without prior OCC approval, Franklin Bank&#8217;s dividend payments in any calendar year are restricted to the bank&#8217;s retained net income for that year, as that term is defined by the laws and regulations, combined with retained net income from the preceding two years, less any required transfer to surplus.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under the Agreement, Franklin Bank was restricted from paying dividends.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank has achieved full compliance with the Agreement, which was terminated in August 2013.</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The OCC and FDIC have authority to limit dividends paid by Franklin Bank, if the payment were determined to be an unsafe and unsound banking practice.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Any payment of dividends that depletes the Bank&#8217;s capital base could be deemed to be an unsafe and unsound banking practice.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under the MOU with the Federal Reserve, MainStreet could not pay any dividends without approval.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The MOU was terminated in September 2013 and there are no longer any restrictions or stipulations attributable to the MOU.</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><I>Branching</I></FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As a national bank, Franklin Bank is required to comply with the state branch banking laws of Virginia, the state in which the Bank is located.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank must also have the prior approval of OCC to establish a branch or acquire an existing banking operation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under Virginia law, Franklin Bank may open branch offices or acquire existing banks or bank branches anywhere in the state.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Virginia law also permits banks domiciled in the state to establish a branch or to acquire an existing bank or branch in another state.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Dodd-Frank Act permits the OCC to approve national bank branches in any state in which a bank located in that state is permitted to establish a branch.</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Monetary Policy</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The monetary and interest rate policies of the Federal Reserve, as well as general economic conditions, affect the business and earnings of MainStreet.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank and other banks are particularly sensitive to interest rate fluctuations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The spread between the interest paid on deposits and that which is charged on loans is the most important component of Franklin Bank&#8217;s profits.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, interest earned on investments held by MainStreet and Franklin Bank has a significant effect on earnings.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As conditions change in the national and international economy and in the money markets, the Federal Reserve&#8217;s actions, particularly with regard to interest rates, can impact loan demand, deposit levels and earnings at Franklin Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It is not possible to accurately predict the effects on MainStreet of economic and interest rate changes.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other Legislative and Regulatory Concerns</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Particularly because of current uncertain and volatile economic conditions as well as recent credit market turmoil and related financial institution concerns, federal and state laws and regulations are likely to be enacted that will affect the regulation of financial institutions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Dodd-Frank Reform Act has been adopted and additional regulations affecting the financial sector have been enacted and additional regulations can be expected, although many of these are not directly applicable to small community financial institutions like MainStreet.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The net effect of these changes in this law as well as others will add to the regulatory burden on banks and increase the costs of compliance, or they could change the products that can be offered and the manner in which banks do business.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We cannot foresee how the additional regulation of financial institutions may change in the future and how those changes might affect MainStreet.</FONT></DIV>

  <TD

<B>Properties</B></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Corporation leases its executive office and operations facility in Martinsville, Virginia.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease commenced on November 19, 2010 for space located at 1075 Spruce Street in Martinsville, Virginia.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease will expire November 30, 2015.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease has an option to renew for one additional five year term.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Franklin Bank&#8217;s main office is located at 400 Old Franklin Turnpike, Suite 100, Rocky Mount, Virginia, in a section of town known as the Rocky Mount Marketplace.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The bank leases a two-story facility with approximately 8,200 square feet of which the Bank provides permanent financing to the owners of which one is a director.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease is for a 15-year period and the expiration date of the lease is June 30, 2018.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease payment mirrors the loan payment plus an 8% return on investment to the owner.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Subject to certain compliance issues, Franklin Bank has the option to extend the lease for one additional term of five years.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If the right to extend this lease for the first renewal term is exercised, Franklin Bank has the right to extend this lease for five additional terms of five years each.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>One of the owners is a director of Franklin Bank and both owners are shareholders of BankShares.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank owns a lot adjacent to their Rocky Mount Office which is utilized for employee parking.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank leases its branch which opened on April 9, 2004 at 12930 Booker T. Washington Highway, Hardy, Virginia.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank provides permanent financing to the owner of this facility.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A director of Franklin<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Bank is a partner in the ownership of this facility.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease commenced on April 7, 2004 and will expire April 6, 2019.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease payment mirrors the loan payment plus an 8% return on investment to the owner.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Subject to certain compliance issues, Franklin Bank has the option to extend the lease for one additional term of five years.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If the right to extend this lease for the first renewal term is exercised, Franklin Bank has the right, or option, to extend or renew this lease for five additional terms of five years each.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank leased its 220 North branch located at 35 Shepherd Drive, Rocky Mount, Virginia.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A director of Franklin Bank was a partner in the ownership of the facility.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease commenced June 1, 2007 and expired June 1, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank closed this banking office effective November 13, 2010; however, the lease remained in effect until its maturity.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank purchased the building at the maturity of the lease and assigned the purchase to another buyer which was a director of both the Corporation and Franklin Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The main office and all branches have a drive-up ATM.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MainStreet RealEstate, Inc. owns the Southlake branch located in the Union Hall area of Franklin County and leases it to Franklin<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The branch opened in August 2007.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The total cost of the land and building were $425,286 and $881,123, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet believes its banking facilities are well located to serve their intended banking markets and are attractively furnished and well equipped for banking purposes.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>All facilities are adequately insured in management&#8217;s opinion.</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Given the injection of $1.3 million into the loan loss reserve by Franklin Bank during the fourth quarter of 2008, MainStreet&#8217;s Board of Directors deemed it prudent to suspend the cash dividend at that time.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The only source of funds for dividends is dividends paid to MainStreet by Franklin Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank is limited in the amount of dividend payments by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, (&#8220;OCC&#8221;), its primary regulator.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The OCC limits annual dividends to a maximum of retained profits of the current year plus the two prior years, without prior OCC approval.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On April 16, 2009, Franklin Bank entered into a formal Agreement (&#8220;Agreement&#8221;) with the OCC.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Among other things, the Agreement required the Bank to adopt a three year capital program and prohibited the payment of a dividend until the Bank achieved compliance with the program and satisfied certain other conditions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank has achieved full compliance with the Agreement, which was terminated in August 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On June 17, 2009, MainStreet entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (&#8220;MOU&#8221;) with the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond, which was amended January 26, 2011.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under the MOU, MainStreet was prohibited from paying any dividends.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The MOU was terminated in September 2013 and there are no longer any restrictions or stipulations attributable to the MOU.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, the payment of future dividends by MainStreet may depend on a return by Franklin Bank to more historical levels of profitability.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Refer to Item 7, Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis for a detailed discussion.</FONT> </FONT></DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following discussion is intended to assist in understanding and evaluating the financial condition and results of operations of MainStreet BankShares, Inc. (&#8220;MainStreet&#8221;, &#8220;BankShares&#8221;, or &#8220;Corporation&#8221;) on a consolidated basis. This discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with BankShares&#8217; consolidated financial statements and related notes included in Item 8 of this report on Form 10-K.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <H1 style="clear:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both"><U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Forward-Looking Statements </FONT></U></H1>  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">This report contains forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those reflected in such forward-looking statements which are representative only on the date hereof.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Readers of this report should not rely solely on the forward-looking statements and should consider all uncertainties and risks discussed throughout this report.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet takes no obligation to update any forward-looking statements contained herein.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Factors that may cause actual results to differ materially from those contemplated by such forward-looking statements include, among others, the following possibilities:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>(1) competitive pressures among depository and other financial institutions may increase significantly; (2) changes in the interest rate environment may reduce margins; (3) general economic conditions, either nationally or regionally, may be less favorable than expected that could result in a deterioration of credit quality or a reduced demand for credit; and (4) legislative or regulatory changes including changes in accounting standards, may adversely affect the business.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">General</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MainStreet was incorporated on January 14, 1999 in the Commonwealth of Virginia and is the bank holding company for Franklin Bank which serves the Franklin County area of Virginia.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet provides a wide variety of banking services through Franklin Bank, which emphasizes personal customer service and other advantages incident to banking with a locally owned community bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It relies on local advertising and the personal contacts of its directors, employees, and shareholders to attract customers and business to the Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank has three banking offices in Rocky Mount and Franklin County.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On February 8, 2007, MainStreet formed a wholly-owned real estate company, MainStreet RealEstate, Inc. for the sole purpose of owning the real estate of the Corporation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet RealEstate, Inc. owns the Union Hall (Southlake) office of Franklin Bank.</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On April 16, 2009, Franklin Bank entered into a formal agreement (&#8220;Agreement&#8221;) with The Comptroller of the Currency (&#8220;OCC&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Agreement required Franklin Bank to perform certain actions within designated time frames.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Agreement was intended to demonstrate the Bank&#8217;s commitment to review/enhance certain aspects of various policies and practices related to credit administration and liquidity.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank achieved full compliance with the Agreement.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Agreement was terminated in August 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On June 17, 2009, MainStreet BankShares, Inc. entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (&#8220;MOU&#8221;) with the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond (&#8220;Federal Reserve&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The MOU required the bank holding company to utilize its financial and managerial resources to assist Franklin Bank in functioning in a safe and sound manner and restricted MainStreet from conducting various activities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On January 26, 2011, we entered into a new MOU with the Federal Reserve which contained the same terms of the previous MOU (which was terminated) but added provisions regarding compliance with certain laws and regulations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This MOU was terminated in September 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>There are no longer any restrictions or stipulations attributable to the MOU.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Critical Accounting Policies</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MainStreet&#8217;s financial statements are prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (GAAP).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The financial information contained within our statements is, to a significant extent, based on measures of </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">the financial effects of transactions and events that have already occurred.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A variety of factors could affect the ultimate value that is obtained either when earning income, recognizing an expense, recovering an asset or relieving a liability. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
<U>  <TABLE
style="WIDTH: 100%">
    <TR>  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="left">
</TD>
  <TD
style="FONT-STYLE: normal; WIDTH: 34%; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom; FONT-WEIGHT: normal" align="middle">
8</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 33%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: bottom" align="right">
</TD>
</TR>
  <TR>  <TD><BR /></TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; BORDER-BOTTOM: #000000 2px solid; FONT-STYLE: normal; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in; HEIGHT: 1px; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 1px" contenteditable="false">
</DIV>
</U>  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Allowance for Loan Losses</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We use historical loss factors, peer comparisons, regulatory factors, concentrations of credit, past dues, and the trend in the economy as factors in determining the inherent loss that may be present in our loan portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Actual losses could differ significantly from the historical factors that we use in estimating risk.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The allowance for loan losses reflects our best estimate of the losses inherent in our loan portfolio. The allowance is based on two basic principles of accounting: (i) losses are accrued when they are probable of occurring and are capable of estimation and (ii) losses are accrued based on the differences between the value of collateral, present value of future cash flows or values that are observable in the secondary market and the loan balance.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The allowance for loan losses is maintained at a level, which, reflects management&#8217;s best estimate of probable credit losses inherent in the loan portfolio and is, therefore, believed to be appropriate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The amount of the allowance is based on management&#8217;s evaluation of the collectability of the loan portfolio, including the nature of the portfolio, credit concentrations, trends in historical loss experience, specific impaired loans, economic conditions and other risks inherent in the portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management reviews the past due reports and risk-rated loans and discusses individually the loans on these reports with the responsible loan officers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management uses these tools and provides a quarterly analysis of the allowance based on our historical loan loss experience, risk-rated loans, past dues, concentrations of credit, unsecured loans, loan exceptions, and the economic trend.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These are generally grouped by homogeneous loan pools.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Impaired loans are reviewed individually to determine possible impairment based on one of three recognized methods which are fair value of collateral, present value of expected cash flows, or observable market price.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A specific reserve is then allocated for the amount of the impairment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Although management uses available information to recognize losses on loans, the substantial uncertainties associated with local economic conditions, collateral values, and future cash flows on impaired loans, make it possible that a material change in the allowance for loan losses in the near term may be appropriate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, the amount of the change cannot be estimated.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The allowance is increased by a provision for loan losses, which is charged to expense, and reduced by charge-offs, net of recoveries.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Changes in the allowance relating to impaired loans are charged or credited to the provision for loan losses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Past due status is determined based on contractual terms.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT><U>Deferred Tax Assets</U></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Corporation uses the asset and liability method of accounting for income taxes.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under this method, deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax bases.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If current available information raises doubt as to the realization of the deferred tax assets, a valuation allowance may be established. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management considers the determination of this valuation allowance to be a critical accounting policy due to the need to exercise significant judgment in evaluating the amount and timing of recognition of deferred tax liabilities and assets, including projections of future taxable income.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">These judgments and estimates are reviewed on a continual basis as regulatory and business factors change.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A valuation allowance for deferred tax assets may be required if the amounts of taxes recoverable through loss carry backs decline, or if we project lower levels of future taxable income.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If such a valuation allowance is deemed necessary in the future, it would be established through a charge to income tax expense that would adversely affect our operating results.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Overview</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">We finished 2013 with a low interest rate environment and near flat loan demand in our market, which has negatively impacted our net interest margin.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Despite these continued challenges and an increase in our nonaccrual loans, we are pleased to report a dramatic improvement in our other real estate properties on our balance sheet.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Our aggressive approach has moved large dollars in foreclosed assets off our balance sheet.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We will continue to maintain an aggressive posture in resolving problem assets as we move into 2014.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We believe this strategy will strengthen the Corporation&#8217;s position and prepare us for future growth.</FONT> </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Total assets at December 31, 2013 and 2012 were $169,031,017 and $183,110,988, respectively, a decline of $14,079,971, or 7.69%.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The composition of the balance sheet has also changed.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The largest components of change were in cash and cash equivalents and loans, net of unearned deferred fees and costs.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Total cash and cash equivalents declined $6.1 million from year-end 2012 while loans, net of unearned deferred fees and costs declined $10.8 million.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loan demand has remained soft during 2013 and we have aggressively continued to work through our problem loans, which has resulted in additional payouts and foreclosures.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Please refer to Footnote #4 for a discussion of our criticized assets.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We continue to monitor our asset quality closely and we have had substantial improvement in the level of our criticized assets, which include loans rated special mention, substandard, doubtful, and loss.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Securities available for sale increased to $21.8 million at year-end 2013 from $18.8 million at year-end 2012 primarily due to purchases in excess of pay downs on mortgage backed securities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This increase was further reduced by calls and sales of securities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Our total deposits declined $7.8 million from year-end 2012 to year-end 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>With the continued focus on lowering our overall deposit costs and soft loan demand, this was an anticipated and expected result.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Our loan to deposit ratio was 86.63% and 89.32% at December 31, 2013 and 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Overall costs of our interest bearing deposits declined 16 basis points in 2013 compared to 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We maintained our relationships as can be evidenced by the increase in demand deposits which are our non-interest bearing funds.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We also had $6.0 million in repurchase agreements mature in January 2013 for which certain securities available for sale were utilized as collateral.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At maturity, we paid off the $6.0 million and now have additional securities that can be utilized and pledged for other purposes, as needed.</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Total shareholders&#8217; equity at December 31, 2013 and 2012 was $23,987,541 and $24,250,373</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">, </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet and Franklin Bank were considered well capitalized at December 31, 2013 and 2012 under the standards of regulatory capital classifications.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The book value of shareholders&#8217; equity at December 31, 2013 and 2012 was $14.00 and $14.15 per share, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'">MainStreet had net income of $205,034 for the year ending December 31, 2013 compared to net income of<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>$1,970,776</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New (W1)'"> for the year ending December 31, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Net income for 2013 was impacted substantially by increased provision expense and reduced income from bank owned life insurance as discussed below, all offset by a decrease in supplemental executive retirement plan (&#8220;SERP&#8221;) expense.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'">Basic and diluted net income per common share was $0.12 and $1.15 for 2013 and 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Return on average assets in 2013 and 2012 was 0</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New (W1)'">.12</FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'">% and 1.02%, respectively while<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> </FONT>return on average shareholders&#8217; equity was 0.85% and 8.69% for 2013 and 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The return on average assets and average equity for 2011 was (0.07%) and (0.66%), respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Year 2013 continued to be impacted by our level of criticized assets.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As we worked through these assets and they moved through the cycle, we experienced losses on the sales of other real estate, write downs associated with lower appraisals and selling prices, and had expenses associated with holding these assets.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>However, these expenses declined by $1,257,198 over 2012 levels.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Provision expense in 2013 was higher than 2012 as we worked through our problem loans and experienced an increase in our net charge offs in the amount of $730,729.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Provision expense for the periods ending December 31, 2013 and 2012 was $1,664,880 and $486,257, respectively.</FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT></FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'">Franklin Bank has two bank owned life insurance policies on the life of<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>its covered current President and Chief Executive Officer.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Upon the tragic death of former CEO Larry A. Heaton in 2012, Franklin Bank collected a death benefit on the bank owned life insurance of approximately $2.4 million.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Also under the Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan (&#8220;SERP&#8221;) upon<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Mr. Heaton&#8217;s death, the present value of the payout of this benefit was accrued and expensed totaling approximately $1 million in 2012.</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Results of Operations</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Net Interest Income</FONT></U></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The low interest rate environment continued during 2013 with the Federal Reserve leaving the short-term interest rates within a range of 0% - .25% which has been effective since 2008.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>At the most recent meeting of the FOMC, the Federal Reserve indicated a slowdown in the purchase of securities due to an improving employment rate.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This change will slowly reverse the QE 3 strategy gradually raising rates over time.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Federal Reserve also indicated they will continue to monitor the economy given its tenuous nature and threat of inflation.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>By employing the QE 3 strategy the Federal Reserve plans to continue purchasing mortgage backed assets at a slower pace. This should slow the effects of the previous Federal Reserve decision to &#8220;twist&#8221; the yield curve by driving up short term rates and lowering long term rates. The net effect is to keep mortgage rates low for an extended period of time to help spur the housing industry and economic growth.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It is also designed to maintain inflation at low levels.</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As interest rates have remained low, our borrowers have extended pressure to move to more fixed rate interest products; however, interest rates on variable rate loans make up approximately 25% of Franklin Bank&#8217;s loan portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In a rising interest rate environment, this initially would have a positive impact on the net interest margin because deposit rates are slower to reprice at the higher rates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In a declining interest rate environment such as we have been in, asset sensitivity initially has had a negative impact on the net interest margin until deposit rates reach an opportunity to reprice.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The addition of floors to segments of our variable rate loan portfolio has helped to control the impact to our net interest margin.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Due to the large amount of repricing deposit liabilities in the near term, the Bank will have a positive impact to the net interest margin in this low interest rate environment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Throughout our history, our overall deposit maturity has been short which has benefited us by allowing us to reprice our deposits downward as they have matured in the lower interest rate environment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On the other hand, in an environment of increasing interest rates, short deposit maturity would reduce the benefit of rising interest rates on loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Furthermore, even though lower interest rates have been beneficial for our cost of deposits, with prime at 3.25% which is the interest rate basis for many of our loans, MainStreet&#8217;s net interest margin has been adversely affected by the prolonged, recessionary low interest rate environment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, competition for deposits remains fierce in our market; however, our goal is to continue to lower our cost of deposits during 2014.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The maturity of our repurchase agreement in September 2012 had a positive impact on our net interest margin for the last quarter of 2012 and continued in 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In addition, the remaining $6 million in repurchase agreements matured in January 2013, which also had a positive impact on our net interest margin.</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160;&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
