<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(e)</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
  <TD
style="WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The recorded investment in loans represents the customers unpaid principal balances, net of partial charge-offs and unearned deferred fees and costs.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Interest on loans is computed by methods which generally result in level rates of return on principal amounts outstanding.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Past due status on all loans is recognized and determined based on contractual terms.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It is the Corporation&#8217;s policy to discontinue the accrual of interest on all loans once they become 90 days past due and are not well-collateralized or earlier when it becomes doubtful that the full principal and interest will be collected.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Generally, all payments for all loans on nonaccrual status are applied as a principal reduction until the principal is satisfied.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As a general rule, a nonaccrual loan may be restored to accrual status when none of its principal and interest is due and unpaid, and the Company expects repayment of the remaining contractual principal and interest.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>If any interest payments received while the loan was in nonaccrual status were applied to reduce the recorded investment in the loan, the application of these payments to the loan&#8217;s recorded investment is not reversed (and interest income is not credited) when the loan is returned to accrual status.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Company must have received repayment of the past due principal and interest unless the asset has been formally restructured and qualifies for accrual status or the borrower has resumed paying the full amount of the scheduled contractual interest and principal payments on a loan that is past due and in nonaccrual status, even though the loan has not been brought fully current, and the following two criteria are met: (1)<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>all principal and interest amounts contractually due (including arrearages) are reasonably assured of repayment within a reasonable period and, (2) there is a sustained period of repayment performance (generally a minimum of six months) by the borrower in accordance with the contractual terms involving payments of cash or cash equivalents.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A loan that meets these two criteria may be restored to accrual status but must continue to be disclosed as past due if all arrearages have not been paid.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">BankShares collectively reviews for impairment all consumer loans and smaller homogeneous loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>BankShares considers a loan to be impaired when, based upon current information and events, it is probable that BankShares will be unable to collect all amounts due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Included in our analysis of<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> impaired loans are loans 90 days or more past due and still accruing, other impaired loans, nonaccrual loans and troubled debt restructurings</FONT> (not on nonaccrual).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>BankShares evaluates its impaired loans and troubled debt restructurings on an individual basis.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For collateral dependent loans, BankShares bases the measurement of these impaired loans on the fair value of the loan&#8217;s collateral properties.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For all other loans, BankShares uses the measurement of these impaired loans on the more readily determinable of the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&#8217;s effective interest rate or the observable market price.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Impairment losses are recognized through an increase in the allowance for loan losses and a corresponding charge to the provision for loan losses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Adjustments to impairment losses due to changes in the fair value of impaired loans are included in the provision for loan losses.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(f)</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
  <TD
style="WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Troubled Debt Restructurings</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="justify">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In situations where, for economic or legal reasons related to a borrower&#8217;s financial condition, management may grant a concession to the borrower that it would not otherwise consider, the related loan is classified as a troubled debt restructuring (&#8220;TDR&#8221;).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management strives to identify borrowers in financial difficulty early and work with them to modify their loan to more affordable terms before their loan reaches nonaccrual status.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These modified terms may include rate reductions, principal forgiveness, payment forbearance and other actions intended to minimize the economic loss and to avoid foreclosure or repossession of the collateral.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>In cases where borrowers are granted new terms that provide for a reduction of either interest or principal, management measures any impairment on the restructuring as noted above for impaired loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Total troubled debt restructurings at December 31, 2013 and 2012 were $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3.9</FONT> million and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">2.2</FONT> million, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>

style="MARGIN-TOP: 0pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0pt; TABLE-LAYOUT: fixed; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; dtth: tableHanging" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <TABLE
style="MARGIN-TOP: 0pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0pt; TABLE-LAYOUT: fixed; CLEAR: both; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; dtth: tableHanging" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%">
    <TR
style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 0pt; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top; PADDING-TOP: 0in">
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 0in; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
</DIV>
</TD>
  <TD
style="WIDTH: 0.5in; WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">(h)</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
  <TD
style="WORD-WRAP: break-word; VERTICAL-ALIGN: top">
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Allowance for Loan Losses</FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The allowance for loan losses is an estimate of the losses that may be sustained in our loan portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The allowance is based on two basic principles of accounting: (1)&#160;losses are accrued when they are probable of occurring and are capable of estimation and (2)&#160;losses are accrued based on the differences between the value of collateral, present value of future cash flows or values that are observable in the secondary market and the loan balance. </FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The allowance for loan losses is maintained at a level, which, in management&#8217;s judgment, is adequate to absorb credit losses inherent in the loan portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The amount of the allowance is based on management&#8217;s evaluation of the collectibility of the loan portfolio, including the nature of the portfolio, credit concentrations, trends in historical loss experience, specific impaired loans, economic conditions, and other risks inherent in the portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As part of this process management reviews the past due reports and risk-rated loans and discusses individually the loans on these reports with the responsible loan officers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management provides a detailed quarterly analysis of the allowance based on our historical loan loss experience, risk-rated loans, past dues, concentrations of credit, unsecured loans, loan exceptions and the economic trend.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These are generally grouped by loan segments. </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our impaired loans are individually reviewed to determine possible impairment based on one of three recognized methods, which are described above.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A specific reserve is then allocated for the amount of the impairment. Possible loss for loans risk rated special mention or lower are then allocated based on a historical loss migration and adjusted for qualitative factors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Remaining loans are pooled based on homogenous loan groups and allocated based on Franklin Bank&#8217;s historical net loss experience.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These pools are as follows:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; (</FONT>1) commercial and industrial loans not secured by real estate; (2) construction and land development loans; (3) residential 1-4 family first liens; (4) residential 1-4 family junior liens; (5) home equity lines; (6) commercial real estate; and (7) consumer or loans to individuals.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Historical loss is calculated based on twelve-quarter average history.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Historical net loss data is adjusted and applied to pooled loans based on qualitative factors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>We utilize the following qualitative factors:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; (</FONT>1) changes in the value of underlying collateral, such as loans not conforming to supervisory loan to value limits; (2) national and local economic conditions; (3) changes in portfolio volume and nature such as borrowers living outside our primary trade area; (4) changes in past dues, nonaccruals; and (5) quality, impact and effects of defined credit concentrations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our allowance methodology has continued to evolve as our Company has grown and our loan portfolio has grown and become more diverse.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Although management uses available information to recognize losses on loans, because of uncertainties associated with local economic conditions, collateral values, and future cash flows on impaired loans, it is reasonably possible that a material change could occur in the allowance for loan losses in the near term; however, this amount cannot be reasonably estimated.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The allowance is increased by a provision for loan losses, which is charged to expense, and reduced by charge-offs, net of recoveries.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Charge-offs on commercial loans are recorded when available information confirms the loan is not fully collectible and the loss is reasonably quantifiable.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Consumer loans are generally charged off for closed end loans after 120 days past due and open end loans after 180 days past due, or earlier if there is information related to a loss.</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans secured by real estate are generally written down to appraised value less liquidation expenses, with the remainder charged-off when a loss is apparent.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Refer to Note 4 of the consolidated financial statements for detailed information related to the allowance for loan losses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>

</TD>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Assets acquired through, or in lieu of, loan foreclosure are held for sale and are initially recorded at the lower of the loan balance or the fair value less costs to sell at the date of foreclosure.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Any losses at this point in time are charged against the allowance for loan losses.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Subsequent to foreclosure, management periodically performs valuations of the foreclosed assets based on updated appraisals, general market conditions, recent sales of like properties, length of time the properties have been held, and our ability and intention with regard to continued ownership of the properties.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Corporation may incur additional write-downs of foreclosed assets to fair value less costs to sell if valuations indicate a further&#160;deterioration in market conditions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These write-downs are recorded in the consolidated statement of income as other real estate and repossessions expense.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Corporation is subject to federal and state income taxes.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The liability (or balance sheet) approach is used in financial accounting and reporting for income taxes.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Deferred income tax assets and liabilities are computed quarterly for differences between the financial statement and tax bases of assets and liabilities that will result in taxable or deductible amounts in the future.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Valuation allowances are established when necessary to reduce deferred tax assets to the amount expected to be realized.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Income tax expense is the tax payable or refundable for the period plus or minus the change during the period in deferred tax assets and liabilities.<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT></B></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">When tax returns are filed, it is highly certain that some positions taken would be sustained upon examination by the taxing authorities, while others are subject to uncertainty about the merits of the position taken or the amount of the position that would be ultimately sustained.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The benefit of a tax position is recognized in the financial statements in the period during which, based on all available evidence, management believes it is more likely than not that the position will be sustained upon examination, including the resolution of appeals or litigation processes, if any.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Tax positions taken are not offset or aggregated with other positions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Tax positions that meet the more-likely-than-not recognition threshold are measured as the largest amount of<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> tax benefit that is more than 50 percent likely of being realized upon settlement with the applicable taxing authority.&#160;</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> </FONT>The portion of the benefits associated with tax positions taken that exceeds the amount measured as described above is reflected as a liability for unrecognized tax benefits in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets along with any associated interest and penalties that would be payable to the taxing authorities upon examination.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Interest and penalties associated with unrecognized tax benefits are classified as additional income taxes in the consolidated statements of income.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Transfers of financial assets are accounted for as sales, when control over the assets has been surrendered.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Control over transferred assets is deemed to be surrendered when (1) the assets have been isolated from the Corporation &#150; put presumptively beyond reach of the transferor and its creditors, even in bankruptcy or other receivership, (2) the transferee obtains the right (free of conditions that constrain it from taking advantage of that right) to pledge or exchange the transferred assets, and (3) the Corporation does not maintain effective control over the transferred assets through an agreement to repurchase them before their maturity or the ability to unilaterally cause the holder to return specific assets.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The presentation of financial statements in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Actual results could differ from those estimates.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Material estimates that are particularly susceptible to significant change in the near term relate to the determination of the allowance for loan losses, the valuation of deferred tax assets, other-than-temporary impairments of securities, valuation of other real estate owned, and the fair value of financial instruments.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>

At</FONT> December 31, 2012, $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.2</FONT> million of securities had unrealized losses<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">, comprised of three securities,</FONT> based on market prices.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Declines in fair value are due to interest rate fluctuations and not due to credit deterioration of the issuers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Corporation does not have any securities that are considered &#8220;other than temporarily impaired&#8221; at December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Federal Reserve Bank stock is included in restricted equity securities and totaled $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">435,100</FONT></FONT> at December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Federal Home Loan Bank (&#8220;FHLB&#8221;) stock makes up the remainder of the balance in restricted equity securities and totaled $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">219,500</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">305,900</FONT> at December 31, 2013 and 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>FHLB stock is generally viewed as a long term investment and as a restricted investment security which is carried at cost, because there is no market for the stock other than the FHLB or member institutions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Therefore, when evaluating FHLB stock for impairment, its value is based on ultimate recoverability of the par value rather than by recognizing temporary declines in value.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Overdrafts reclassified to loans at December 31, 2013 and 2012 were $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">6,196</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">5,287</FONT>, respectively.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loan Origination/Risk Management</FONT></U></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank&#8217;s Board of Directors annually approves and reviews policies and procedures to be utilized as tools by account officers for the purpose of making sound and prudent credit decisions.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Every loan transaction is closely evaluated from the perspective of profitability realizing that there is no profit in a loan that becomes a loss.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Each credit decision is based on merit and no other factors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Account officers carry a heavy burden of accountability in being assigned the responsibility for the development of the Corporation&#8217;s loan portfolio by meeting the legitimate credit needs of our customers while also exercising prudence and seasoned judgment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A comprehensive reporting system has been developed to provide senior management timely information related to portfolio performance including growth, delinquency, adversely risk rated, and credit concentrations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The portfolio is constantly reviewed based on segments of concern, past due status, extension of credits along with stress testing the portfolio&#8217;s collateral values and debt service coverage for a significant portion of loans within defined loan concentrations. <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT>Annually, a loan review plan is developed to identify and mitigate potential weakness in the loan portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Scope is determined based upon a risk assessment of various concentrations and loan product types in which higher risk may exist.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The developed plan is presented to the Loan Committee of Franklin Bank&#8217;s Board of Directors each year for approval.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Overall, the goal for 2013 was to review <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">30</FONT>% of the entire loan portfolio.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Review segments vary from year to year to ensure a complete cycle of all significant loan product types.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Results of each review segment are communicated to the Loan Committee of the Board of Directors with a response from the Bank&#8217;s Senior Lender or Head of Retail lending depending on the product type reviewed.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In general all loans exceeding $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">100,000</FONT> are documented by three years of financial reports in conjunction with review and analysis by a credit analyst independent of the lending approval process.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>Generally all real estate loans are underwritten based on verified income, or cash flow, and margined at <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">80</FONT>% or less depending upon the regulatory supervisory limit. All loans are underwritten based upon analysis of all identified primary and secondary repayment sources.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Construction &amp; Land Development</FONT></U></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: Emphasis is placed on the estimated absorption period of the project based on the intimate knowledge of local demand and geographic concentrations by appraisers and account officers.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Projects are monitored by Franklin Bank&#8217;s in-house construction inspector to ensure adherence to project specifications and timely completion.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loan to values are manually tracked to ensure conforming collateral coverage is maintained throughout the development phase. Interest carry abilities are determined by analyzing global cash flow and available liquidity.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Due to the complex nature of loans for speculative housing and speculative lots, requests are underwritten by Franklin Bank&#8217;s business lending group.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Terms at origination for speculative lot loans are based on collateral margins and on qualifying the borrower to policy requirements based on a ten year amortization period.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Speculative housing terms generally are held to eighteen months with allowance made for substantial curtailments.</FONT></DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <DIV

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">December 31, 2013 and 2012</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="TEXT-DECORATION: none">&#160;</FONT></FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Commercial Real Estate</FONT></U></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: Loans are generally underwritten based on verified income or cash flow to ensure a global debt service coverage ratio of at least <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.25</FONT>. In general, collateral margin is determined based on appraisal or evaluation of&#160;market value not to exceed <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">80</FONT> percent of appraised market value or cost, whichever is less.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>All properties receive proper environmental due diligence prior to funding of the credit.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Account officers perform and document a market analysis which may include data on competing businesses and projects.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>When applicable, market analysis data may be obtained from independent sources.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>Cash flows and collateral margins are appropriately stress tested.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Terms generally range from five to fifteen years, however, may be longer based on approval from Franklin Bank&#8217;s President or Senior Lender.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Commercial Loans</FONT></U></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans are generally underwritten based on verified income or cash flow to ensure global debt service coverage ratio of at least <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.25</FONT>. Terms can range up to seven years based on loan purpose and collateral offered.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Based on policy, credit lines have maturities of one year.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Generally inventory loans are margined at <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">50</FONT>% while equipment loans, depending on age of collateral, range from <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">90</FONT>%, if new, to <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">80</FONT>%, if used.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>Receivables are margined at <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">80</FONT>% based on the aging of receivables outstanding sixty days or less.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Consumer /Residential 1-4 Families and Equity Lines</FONT></U></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">:<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loans are generally underwritten based on a maximum debt to income ratio of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">40</FONT> percent gross.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>Incomes are verified for all secured loans exceeding $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">35,000</FONT> and unsecured loans totaling $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">10,000</FONT> or more.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Policy requires income verification to be documented for all real estate loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;&#160; </FONT>Collateral margins and terms for non-real estate collateral are determined and made available to retail lenders by Franklin Bank&#8217;s Senior Lender.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Cash flows for all self employed borrowers are determined by Franklin Bank&#8217;s independent credit analyst.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Policy defines unsecured loan terms at a maximum of thirty six months while individual unsecured lines are underwritten to maturities of less than one year with the line amount being based on a percentage of available liquidity and net worth.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Construction loans for individuals are underwritten to policy based on cost overruns of at least fifteen percent.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Debt to income ratios for equity lines are underwritten based on the borrower paying <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.5</FONT>% of the total available line monthly.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>All equity lines are reviewed annually and filtered based on updated credit scores, average percentage drawn and delinquency. &#8220;Watch&#8221; accounts are identified based on filters and then individually reviewed by the responsible account officer.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">

style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">At December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012, the balance in loans under the terms of troubled debt restructurings not included in nonaccrual loans was $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1,929,999</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1,305,180</FONT>, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These loans did not have any additional commitments at December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Corporation assesses all loan modifications to determine whether they are considered troubled debt restructurings (TDRs).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Loan restructurings generally occur when a borrower is experiencing, or is expected to experience, financial difficulties in the near-term.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Consequently, a modification that would otherwise not be considered is granted to the borrower.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>These loans may continue to accrue interest as long as the borrower complies with the revised terms and conditions and has demonstrated repayment performance with the modified terms.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The borrowers were complying with the modified terms of their contracts at December 31, 2013 and December 31, 2012, respectively.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Troubled debt restructurings are included in the impaired loan disclosures.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">During the year ended December 31, 2013, the Corporation modified five loans that were considered to be TDRs, of which one is on nonaccrual.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Two of the commercial loans were the renewals of credit designated as a TDR.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The last commercial note was the restructure of a stale line of credit, of which part of the credit was restructured to a term note.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This credit belongs to a former director who resigned in February 2014.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Corporation lowered the payment on one of the commercial real estate credits, which extended the amortization out of policy guidelines, in order to allow the borrower time to attract new tenants.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The second commercial real estate credit was a result of charging off part of the original credit and positioning the credit and borrowers with the ability to go forward with a performing credit.</FONT></DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There were no troubled debt restructurings modified during the prior twelve months that defaulted during the year ended December 31, 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For this purpose, if a note defaults it means at some point it has been greater than 60 days past due or we have received some information that leads us to believe the full collection of the principal and interest is doubtful.</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">One of the commercial loans restructured was a renewal of an existing loan for a short period of time to allow the borrower to come up with an action plan.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The borrower&#8217;s debt service ratio had declined moving the credit to a criticized asset.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The second commercial loan was restructured to interest only to lower the payment to allow the borrower time to receive their inheritance.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The first construction and land development loan was the renewal of a criticized credit for a short term to allow the borrower to sell assets.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The second construction and land development loan was restructured to obtain additional collateral and reduce impairment.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The third construction and land development loan was restructured to give the borrower additional time to have an auction in the spring to sell properties.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The loan was modified to interest only.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The residential 1-4 family loan was modified to gain additional collateral and allow the borrower to improve cash flow.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The commercial real estate loan was the restructure of a stale line of credit into an amortizing loan of a criticized asset.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There were no troubled debt restructurings modified during the prior twelve months that defaulted during the year ended December 31, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For this purpose, if a note defaults it means at some point it has been greater than 60 days past due or we have received some information that leads us to believe the full collection of the principal and interest is doubtful.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Corporation&#8217;s internally assigned grades for credit quality are as follows:</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 50%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 50%; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Prime (1.00)</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Exceptional credits are of the highest quality. These loans are supported by large, well-established borrowers with excellent financial stability and strength, and may be secured by cash or cash equivalents.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Where applicable, guarantors have substantial net worth and personal cash flow, and could easily fulfill their obligation should the need arise.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 50%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 50%; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Good (2.00)</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Superior credits are supported by well-established borrowers with excellent financial stability and strength. The borrower&#8217;s cash flow, liquidity, and equity are more than ample. These credits may be secured by cash or cash equivalents.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For loans with personal guarantees, the guarantors are high net worth individuals, and have the resources available to satisfy their obligation if necessary.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;LINE-HEIGHT: 50%; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 0.5in; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 50%; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Acceptable (3.00)</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans in this category are supported by borrowers and guarantors that are financially sound.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Cash flow, liquidity and equity are sufficient to provide a comfortable margin in the event of short-term economic disturbances.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Assets pledged as collateral would provide a dependable secondary source of repayment.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Pass/Watch (4.00)</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Credits in this category present the maximum acceptable risk for new facilities.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Borrowers generate enough cash for debt service needs, but may not have sufficient resources to weather short-term market fluctuations.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Management may lack depth or experience, and industry volatility may be an issue. <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT>Where applicable, guarantors have sufficient resources to provide an additional margin of protection.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Special Mention (5.00)</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Assets in this category demonstrate signs of potential weakness, which, if uncorrected, could result in default.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The borrower&#8217;s </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">liquidity or equity may be marginal, trends in cash flow and profitability may point to a weakening financial condition, or the borrower&#8217;s industry may be slightly unstable or showing early indications of decline. Collateral may be illiquid or provide only a relatively small margin.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Migration analysis data is performed and updated quarterly on these loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It is based on loans downgraded originally into this category.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Our loss factor is determined based on charge-offs during the quarter divided by the balance of special mention loans at the beginning of the quarter, which is then increased by qualitative factors resulting in an applied loss factor of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3</FONT>%.</FONT></DIV>

  <DIV

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">December 31, 2013 and 2012</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Substandard (6.00)</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans in this category present an unacceptable credit risk.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Borrowers and guarantors may be financially weak, and may lack the sufficient resources to adequately service debt. The abilities of management and industry stability may also be of concern.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Collateral may be lacking in quality or liquidity, and offers little additional protection.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Migration analysis data is performed and updated quarterly on these loans.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>It is based on loans downgraded originally into this category.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>For non-impaired substandard loans, our loss factor is determined based on charge-offs during the quarter divided by the balance of substandard loans at the beginning of the quarter.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This is then increased by the substandard loans&#8217; qualitative factors resulting in an applied loss factor of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">8</FONT>%.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Doubtful (7.00)</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">These loans have an extremely high probability of loss, though the timing and magnitude of the loss may remain unclear.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Borrowers and guarantors exhibit major financial shortcomings, and clearly lack the sufficient resources to adequately service the debt or honor their commitments. Collateral is lacking in quality or liquidity, and offers little, if any, additional protection.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loss (8.00)</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The probability of collection on these credits is so low that they may be properly classified as uncollectible. </FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Generally, consumer loans, home equity lines, and residential 1-4 family loans are not risk rated and are considered a pass credit unless they are related to a risk rated commercial loan relationship or exhibit criticized asset characteristics.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Corporation has a lease agreement for its facility in Martinsville, Virginia.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>MainStreet&#8217;s executive office and operations area lease, which commenced on <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">November 19, 2010</FONT>, is for <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">7,900</FONT> square feet of space located at 1075 Spruce Street in Martinsville, Virginia.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease will expire <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">November 30, 2015</FONT></FONT>.</FONT>   <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Franklin Bank&#8217;s main office is located at 400 Old Franklin Turnpike, Suite 100, Rocky Mount, Virginia, in a section of town known as the Rocky Mount Marketplace.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The bank leases a two-story facility with approximately <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">8,200</FONT> square feet of which </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">the Bank provides permanent financing to the owners, of which one is a director.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease is for a <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">15</FONT>-year period and the expiration date of the lease is <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">June 30, 2018</FONT>.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease payment mirrors the loan payment plus an <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">8</FONT>% return on investment to the owner.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>One of the owners is also a director of Franklin Bank and both owners are shareholders of BankShares.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A banking office, Westlake Branch, of Franklin Bank opened on April 9, 2004 at 12930 Booker T. Washington Highway, Hardy, Virginia.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The bank also provides permanent financing to the owner of this facility, of which a director of the bank is a partner.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease commenced on <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">April 7, 2004</FONT> and will expire <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">April 6, 2019</FONT>.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease payment mirrors the loan payment plus an <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">8</FONT>% return on investment to the owner.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank&#8217;s 220 North banking office was located at 35 Shepherd Drive, Rocky Mount, Virginia.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>A director of Franklin Bank was a partner in the ownership of the facility.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The lease commenced June 1, 2007 and expired June 1, 2012.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>This banking office was closed effective November 13, 2010; however, the lease remained in effect until its maturity and had a sublease until then.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank purchased the building at the maturity of the lease and assigned the purchase to another buyer who was a director of both the Corporation and Franklin Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></DIV>

  <H4 style="clear:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Note 14 - Stock Options and Warrants</FONT></B></H4>  <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The shareholders of MainStreet approved the 2004 Key Employee Stock Option Plan, (the &#8220;Plan&#8221;), at its Annual Meeting on April 15, 2004.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Plan permitted the grant of Non-Qualified Stock Options and Incentive Stock Options to persons designated as &#8220;Key Employees&#8221; of BankShares or its subsidiaries.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The Plan was approved by the Board of Directors on<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>January 21, 2004 and terminated on January 21, 2009, except with respect to awards made prior to and outstanding on that date which remain valid in accordance with their terms.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Option awards were granted with an exercise price equal to the market value of MainStreet&#8217;s stock at the date of grant.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The options issued in 2007 and 2006 had a vesting period of <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">3</FONT> years and have </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">a ten year contractual term.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The options issued in 2005 vested immediately upon grant and have a ten year contractual term.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>All share awards provide for accelerated vesting if there is a change in control (as defined in the Plan).<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The maximum number of shares that could have been issued under the Plan could not exceed <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">150,700</FONT>.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As of December 31, 2013, there were <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">136,527</FONT> options granted under this Plan of which <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">822</FONT> options have been exercised, <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">61,249</FONT> options have expired, and <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">7,433</FONT> stock options forfeited.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MAINSTREET BANKSHARES, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
<FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 115%; FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">December 31, 2013 and 2012</FONT></FONT></H5>  <H5 style="clear:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center"><B></B>&#160;</H5>  <H5 style="clear:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Note 15 &#150; Regulatory Requirements and Restrictions</FONT></B></H5>  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman','serif'">The payment of dividends to the shareholders is significantly dependent on the ability of the subsidiary bank to pay dividends to the Corporation. </FONT>Under the applicable federal laws, the Comptroller of the Currency restricts the total dividend payments of any calendar year, without prior approval, to the net profits of that year as defined, combined with retained net profits for the two preceding years.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As of December 31, 2013, the aggregate amount of unrestricted funds according to the regulation that could be transferred from the Corporation&#8217;s bank subsidiary to the Parent Corporation for payment of dividends to shareholders without prior regulatory approval, totaled $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1,879,805</FONT> or <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1.11</FONT>% of the total consolidated assets.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>On April 16, 2009, Franklin Bank entered into a formal agreement with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency that restricted dividend payments to the holding company.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank has achieved full compliance with the Agreement, which was terminated in August 2013.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT></FONT></FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Franklin Bank is a member of the Federal Reserve System; however, Franklin Bank processes daily through a correspondent bank, Community Bankers&#8217; Bank.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>As of December 31, 2013, Franklin Bank was required to maintain a reserve balance of $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">250,000</FONT> with Community Bankers&#8217; Bank.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Franklin Bank is subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by the federal and state banking agencies.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Failure to meet minimum capital ratios can initiate certain mandatory, and possibly additional discretionary actions by regulators that, if undertaken, could have a material effect on the consolidated financial statements.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Under capital adequacy guidelines and the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action, Franklin Bank must meet specific capital guidelines that involve quantitative measures of their assets, liabilities and certain off-balance sheet items as calculated under regulatory accounting practices.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>The capital amounts and classification are also subject to qualitative judgments by the regulators about components, risk weightings, and other factors.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Quantitative measures established by regulations to ensure capital adequacy require Franklin Bank to maintain minimum capital ratios.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>Franklin Bank was well-capitalized at December 31, 2013 and 2012.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"></FONT>&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">As of December 31, 2013, the most recent notification from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation categorized the Bank as well capitalized under the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>To be categorized as well capitalized, an institution must maintain minimum total risk-based, Tier 1 risk-based and Tier 1 leverage ratios as set forth in the following tables.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160; </FONT>There are no conditions or events since the notification that management believes have changed the Bank&#8217;s category.<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"></FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

  <H5 style="clear:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Note 17 &#150; Financial Instruments With Off-Balance-Sheet Risk</FONT></B></H5>  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of its customers, BankShares is a party to financial instruments with off-balance-sheet risk. These financial instruments involve commitments to extend credit. These instruments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit risk in excess of the amount recognized in the consolidated balance sheets.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>

62</TD>

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Corporation&#8217;s exposure to credit loss in the event of nonperformance by the other party to the financial instruments for commitments to extend credit is represented by the contractual amount of those instruments. The same credit policy is used in making commitments as is used for on-balance-sheet risk. At December 31, 2013 and 2012, outstanding commitments to extend credit including letters of credit were $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">17,681,657</FONT> and $<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">15,726,309</FONT> respectively.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">There are no commitments to extend credit on impaired loans. Commitments to extend credit are agreements to lend to a customer as long as there is no breach of any condition established in the contract. Commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses and may require payment of a fee. The commitments may expire without ever being drawn upon, therefore, the total commitment amounts do not necessarily represent future cash outlays for the Corporation.</FONT></DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Note 18 &#150; Concentrations of Credit Risk</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MainStreet monitors its loan portfolio by the segments found in Note 3 of these financial statements. In addition, we look </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">at the trends of significant industries within the segments. Loan segments are categorized primarily based upon regulatory guidelines which follow the underlying collateral. For the most part, MainStreet&#8217;s business activity is with customers located in our primary market area. Accordingly, operating results are closely correlated with the economic trends within the region and influenced by the significant regional industries within the region including pre-built housing, real estate development, agricultural, and resort and leisure services. In addition, the ultimate collectability of the loan portfolio is susceptible to changes in the market condition of the region. The real estate market in our area is also affected by the national economy because a portion of our real estate lending is dependent on buyers who move into our region. There are three industry concentrations that are broken out in the table below by our loan segments.</FONT></DIV>

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MainStreet has established policies related to the credit process and collateral in loan originations. Loans to purchase real and personal property are generally collateralized by the related property with loan amounts established based on certain percentage limitations of the property&#8217;s total stated or appraised value. Credit approval is primarily a function of cash flow, collateral and the evaluation of the creditworthiness of the individual borrower or project based on pertinent financial information and the amount to be financed.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: 'Times New Roman'; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MainStreet has established policies for correspondent bank risk to include cash and due from accounts and overnight federal funds sold. Correspondents are monitored on a quarterly basis, and more frequently if warranted, on several financial and credit ratios. Total exposure is evaluated.&#160;</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Generally accepted accounting principles specify a hierarchy of valuation techniques based on whether the inputs to those valuation techniques are observable or unobservable. Observable inputs reflect market data obtained from independent sources, while unobservable inputs reflect MainStreet&#8217;s market assumptions. The three levels of the fair value hierarchy based on these two types of inputs are as follows:</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following describes the valuation techniques used by MainStreet to measure certain financial assets and liabilities recorded at fair value on a recurring basis in the consolidated financial statements:</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Securities available for sale</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: Securities available for sale are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis. Fair value measurement is based upon quoted market prices, when available (Level 1). If quoted market prices are not available, fair values are measured utilizing independent valuation techniques of identical or similar securities for which significant assumptions are derived primarily from or corroborated by observable market data. Third party vendors compile prices from various sources and may determine the fair value of identical or similar securities by using pricing models that consider observable market data (Level 2). We only utilize third party vendors to provide fair value data for the purposes of recording amounts related to our fair value measurements of our securities available for sale portfolio. We obtain SSAE16 reports from our third party vendor on an annual basis. Our third party vendor also utilizes a reputable pricing company for security market data that utilizes a matrix pricing model. For government sponsored agencies, the model gathers information from market sources and integrates relative credit information, observed market movements and sector news. For agency mortgage backed securities, the model incorporates the current weighted average maturity and takes into account additional pool level information supplied directly by the agency or government sponsored enterprise. The third party vendor system has controls and edits in place for month-to-month market checks and zero pricing. We make no adjustments to the pricing service data received for our securities available for sale.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">

  <DIV

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Certain assets are measured at fair value on a nonrecurring basis in accordance with GAAP. Adjustments to the fair value of these assets usually result from the application of lower-of-cost-or-market accounting or write-downs of individual assets.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The following describes the valuation techniques used by MainStreet to measure certain assets recorded at fair value on a nonrecurring basis in the financial statements:</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Loans Held for Sale</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: Loans held for sale are recorded at fair value on a nonrecurring basis which is the carrying value. Loans held for sale, generally, are closed and sold within two weeks.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Impaired Loans</FONT></U><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">: Loans are designated as impaired when, in the judgment of management based on current information and events, it is probable that all amounts due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement will not be collected. The measurement of loss associated with impaired loans can be based on either the observable market price of the loan or the fair value of the collateral. Fair value is measured based on the value of the collateral securing the loans or the present value of future cash flows. Collateral may be in the form of real estate or business assets including equipment, inventory, and accounts receivable. The vast majority of the collateral is real estate. The value of real estate collateral is determined utilizing recent appraisals conducted by an independent, licensed appraiser outside of MainStreet using observable market data (Level 2). However, if the appraisal of the real estate property is not current, or has been discounted, then the fair value is considered Level 3. It is also considered Level 3 if an evaluation is conducted by Franklin Bank, rather than by a third party. The value of business equipment is based upon an outside appraisal if deemed significant, or the net book value on the&#160;financial statements of the applicable business, if not considered significant using observable market data. Likewise, values for inventory and accounts receivables collateral are based on financial statement balances or aging reports (Level 3). Impaired loans allocated to the Allowance for Loan Losses are measured at fair value on a nonrecurring basis. Any fair value adjustments are recorded in the period incurred as provision for loan losses on the Consolidated Statements of Income.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Other Real Estate Owned (OREO): Foreclosed assets are adjusted to fair value upon transfer of the loans to OREO. Subsequently, OREO is carried at the lower of carrying value or fair market value less selling costs. Fair value is based upon independent market prices, appraised values of the collateral or management&#8217;s estimation of the value of the collateral. When the fair value of the collateral is based on a recent appraisal conducted by an independent licensed appraiser using observable market data, the Corporation records the OREO as nonrecurring Level 2. When the appraisal of the real estate property is not current, or has been discounted, the Corporation records the OREO as nonrecurring Level 3. It is also considered Level 3 if an evaluation is conducted by Franklin Bank, rather than by a third party. Any fair value adjustments are recorded as other real estate and repossessions expense on the Consolidated Statements of Income.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><B><U>Loans</U></B></FONT></DIV>
</TD>
</TR>
</TABLE>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 27pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Fair values are estimated for portfolios of loans with similar financial characteristics. Loans are segregated by type such as commercial, real estate &#150; commercial, real estate &#150; construction, real estate &#150; mortgage and other consumer.&#160;Each loan category is further segmented into fixed and adjustable rate interest terms and by performing and nonperforming categories. The fair value of performing loans is calculated by discounting scheduled cash flows through the estimated maturity using estimated market discount rates that reflect the credit and interest rate risk inherent in the loan as well as estimates for operating expenses and prepayments. The estimate of maturity is based on management&#8217;s assumptions with repayment for each loan classification, modified, as required, by an estimate of the effect of current economic and lending conditions.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MAINSTREET BANKSHARES, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV

  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">December 31, 2013 and 2012</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both" align="center">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Fair value estimates are made at a specific point in time, based on relevant market information about the financial instrument. These estimates do not reflect any premium or discount that could result from offering for sale at one time the Corporation&#8217;s entire holdings of a particular financial instrument. Because no market exists for a significant portion of the Corporation&#8217;s financial instruments, fair value estimates are based on judgments regarding future expected loss experience, current economic conditions, risk characteristics of various financial instruments and other factors. These estimates are subjective in nature and </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">involve uncertainties and matters of significant judgment and therefore, cannot be determined with precision. Changes in assumptions could significantly affect the estimates. Fair value estimates are based on existing on-and-off-balance sheet&#160;financial instruments without attempting to estimate the value of anticipated future business and the value of assets and liabilities that are not considered financial instruments.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">The Corporation assumes interest rate risk (the risk that general interest rate levels will change) as a result of its normal operations. As a result, the fair values of the Corporation&#8217;s financial instruments will change when interest rate levels change and that change may be either favorable or unfavorable to the Corporation. Management attempts to match maturities of assets and liabilities to the extent believed necessary to minimize interest rate risk. However, borrowers with fixed rate obligations are less likely to prepay in a rising rate environment and more likely to prepay in a falling rate environment. Conversely, depositors who are receiving fixed rates are more likely to withdraw funds before maturity in a rising rate environment and less likely to do so in a falling rate environment. Management monitors rates and maturities of assets and liabilities and attempts to minimize interest rate risk by adjusting terms of new loans and deposits and by investing in securities with terms that mitigate the Corporation&#8217;s overall interest rate risk.</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both">
</DIV>
<BR />  <DIV  name="SectionRPT324201415355PM"
style="CLEAR:both;CLEAR: both;clear:both;">

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Note 22 &#150; Regulatory</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On April 16, 2009, Franklin Bank entered into a formal agreement (&#8220;Agreement&#8221;) with The Comptroller of the Currency (&#8220;OCC&#8221;). The Agreement required Franklin Bank to perform certain actions within designated time frames. The Agreement was intended to demonstrate Franklin Bank&#8217;s commitment to review/enhance certain aspects of various policies and practices related to credit administration and liquidity. Franklin Bank achieved full compliance with the Agreement. The Agreement was terminated in August 2013.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">On June 17, 2009, MainStreet BankShares, Inc. entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (&#8220;MOU&#8221;) with the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond (&#8220;Federal Reserve&#8221;). The MOU required the bank holding company to utilize its financial and managerial resources to assist Franklin Bank in functioning in a safe and sound manner and restricted MainStreet from conducting various activities. On January 26, 2011, we entered into a new MOU with the Federal Reserve which contained the same terms of the previous MOU (which was terminated) but added provisions regarding compliance with certain laws and regulations. This MOU was terminated in September 2013. There are no longer any restrictions or stipulations attributable to the MOU.</FONT></DIV>

<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">MainStreet&#8217;s principal executive officer and principal financial officer have reviewed MainStreet&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in 204.13a-15(e) and 204.15d-15(e)) as of the end of the period covered by this annual report and based on their evaluation believe that MainStreet&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures are effective.   <DIV

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV

<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">To the Stockholders:</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></B></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management is responsible for the preparation and fair presentation of the financial statements included in this annual report. The financial statements have been prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America and reflect management&#8217;s judgments and estimates concerning effects of events and transactions that are accounted for or disclosed.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Management is also responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting. The Corporation&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that pertain to the Corporation&#8217;s ability to record, process, summarize and report reliable financial data. Management recognizes that there are inherent limitations in the effectiveness of any internal control over financial reporting, including the possibility of human error and the circumvention or overriding of internal control. Accordingly, even effective internal control over financial reporting can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparation. Further, because of changes in conditions, the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting may vary over time.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
&#160;</DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">In order to ensure that the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting is effective, management regularly assesses such controls and did so most recently for its financial reporting as of December 31, 2013. This assessment was based on criteria for effective internal control over financial reporting described in <I>Internal Control Integrated</I> <I>Framework</I> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations (COSO) of the Treadway Commission in 1992. Based on this assessment, management has concluded that the internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 31, 2013.</FONT></DIV>
  <DIV
style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">&#160;</FONT></DIV>

style="CLEAR:both;MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt; CLEAR: both">
<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">This annual report does not include an attestation report of the Company&#8217;s independent registered public accounting firm regarding internal control over financial reporting. Management&#8217;s report was not subject to attestation by the Company&#8217;s independent registered public accounting firm pursuant to the Securities and Exchange Commission final rule effective September 21, 2010 providing this requirement shall not apply with respect to any audit report prepared for an issuer that is neither an accelerated filer nor a large accelerated filer as defined in Rule 12b-2 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.</FONT></DIV>
